title: You are being pushed to sign something now
lede: A settlement agreement, a lease, a loan, a franchise deal, a freelance contract. It is long, you have been given ten minutes, and the person handing it to you keeps saying it is standard.

blocks.text: A settlement agreement, a lease, a loan, a franchise deal, a freelance contract. It is long, you have been given ten minutes, and the person handing it to you keeps saying it is standard.

items: Urgency around signature is almost always a construction. A document worth signing survives twenty-four hours; one that does not, tells you what it is.
"Standard" is a persuasion word, not a legal category. Standard for whom is the question.
The clauses that matter are rarely the ones being discussed: termination, penalties, automatic renewal, exclusivity, personal guarantees, and what happens if you want out.
A personal guarantee is the single most consequential thing hiding in ordinary business paperwork. It pierces the company and reaches your house.

items.move: Refuse to sign in the room, once, calmly
items.detail: This is the entire skill. Everything else is detail.

items.move: Take the document away, or photograph every page
items.detail: You cannot review what you cannot read later, and unsigned copies get withdrawn.

items.move: Read the exit terms first, then the money
items.detail: Notice period, penalties, renewal, and how you get out. Read those before the headline figure.

items.move: Search for the specific clauses that bite
items.detail: Personal guarantee, indemnity, liquidated damages, non-compete, arbitration, auto-renewal, sole and exclusive.
Most terms are negotiable and most people never ask. Asking is free and it is expected.

items.move: Get one hour of professional review for anything material
items.detail: A lawyer for an hour costs a fraction of one bad clause. For settlement agreements the other side often pays for your advice.

items.say: "I do not sign anything on the day I first see it. Send it over and I will come back with any questions by Thursday."
"I am sure it is standard for you. It is not standard for me, so I am going to read it properly."
"I am comfortable with everything except clause 9. Remove the personal guarantee and I will sign today."
"If the offer depends on me not reading it, that answers my question."

items: Signing to avoid an awkward silence. That silence is a technique.
Relying on a verbal assurance that a clause "will never be enforced." The document is what is enforced.
Initialling pages "just to acknowledge receipt" without knowing what you are acknowledging.
Signing a settlement agreement without independent advice — in many places it is not even valid without it.
Giving a personal guarantee to keep a deal alive. Walk instead.
Keep a countersigned copy plus every version and email. Negotiation history matters if there is a dispute.
Diary the key dates: notice deadlines, renewal dates, review points. Auto-renewal traps run on forgotten dates.
Note who promised what verbally, and when — and get it added in writing before signature.
If you already signed under pressure, check for cooling-off rights immediately. They often exist and they expire.

limit: Never sign under time pressure. If you are told the offer expires today, that is information about the offer, not about you. For anything involving your home, your pension, a guarantee, or a debt secured on property, get independent legal or regulated financial advice first — and check the firm on the official register yourself.
